The same FR-15 content (compact-open dual, local compactness, compact/discrete duality, duals of Z, R/Z, R and finite products) was recovered independently in full from Dikranjan §§7.1-7.3, Loomis §§34-35 and Einsiedler-Ward Appendix C.3, and is carried by the local proofs on this A page.

alternatives.argument: Dikranjan, Theorem 7.2(c) proves in full that the compact-open topology makes the dual a topological group (with the addition estimates of 7.2(d)); Loomis 34D proves continuity of pointwise multiplication from the compact-open basis U(C,eps,a0) and notes that the inverse is pointwise. Both are for T = R/Z and carry over verbatim through the topological-group isomorphism with the multiplicative unit circle.

Dikranjan, Theorem 7.2(f2)-(f3) and Theorem 7.14 prove that a neighbourhood {chi : chi(U) subset Lambda4} of the identity in the dual has compact closure when U is relatively compact, using the arc criterion 7.2(a) and a compactness argument in the product of all homomorphisms; the local item reconstructs the same step with the published Ascoli-Arzela theorem and equicontinuity on a compact neighbourhood.

Dikranjan, Example 7.1(1)-(2) proves both implications: for compact G the set W(G, Lambda1) equals {0} because Lambda1 contains no nontrivial subgroup of T, and for discrete G the compact-open topology is the product topology on Hom(G,T), which is closed in the compact product T^G. Einsiedler-Ward, Lemma C.7 states the same dichotomy with an L1-orthogonality proof.

row.name: C.3, Theorem C.10 and Theorem C.12: inversion and Pontryagin biduality
row.reason: Inversion and biduality are the subjects of the planned Bochner/inversion and duality pairs; the FR-15 foundation is deliberately inversion-free.

row.name: C.3, Theorem C.10 (printed p. 436): Fourier inversion on L1(G) intersect B(G)
row.reason: The actual EW inversion theorem concerns a Haar Fourier transform and the positive-definite class B(G); FR15 constructs the dual topologically without an inversion assertion. FR16 is the approved inversion destination.

row.name: C.3, Theorem C.12 (printed p. 437): the evaluation map G to its bidual is an LCA isomorphism
row.reason: The actual EW biduality theorem asserts evaluation-map surjectivity for every LCA group. FR15 supplies joint evaluation and elementary duals but no general double-dual identification; FR17 is the approved biduality destination.
